seed: Random seed for sampling. Use a fixed value for reproducible outputs. 4294967295 (-1) means a random seed each time.
temperature: Controls randomness. Lower values (0.1-0.5) make output focused and deterministic; higher values (>1) make it more creative and unpredictable. 0 is greedy decoding.
dynatemp_range: Dynamic temperature range. The temperature varies within [temperature - range, temperature + range] depending on token confidence. 0 disables dynamic temperature.
dynatemp_exponent: Shapes how dynamic temperature scales with token entropy. Only used when Dynatemp Range is above 0. Higher values change the curve more sharply.
top_k: Limits selection to the K most likely tokens. Lower values give safer, more predictable text; 0 disables the limit.
top_p: Nucleus sampling. Picks from the smallest set of tokens whose combined probability reaches this value. Lower values give more focused output; 1.0 disables it.
min_p: Discards tokens whose probability is below this fraction of the most likely token's probability. Higher values give safer output; 0 disables it.
top_n_sigma: Keeps only tokens within N standard deviations of the top logit. Lower values give stricter filtering. -1 disables it.
xtc_probability: Chance (0-1) that XTC (Exclude Top Choices) is applied per token. XTC removes the most likely tokens to boost creativity. 0 disables it.
xtc_threshold: Probability threshold for XTC. When two or more tokens are above it, the top ones may be excluded. Lower values make XTC trigger more often. Only used when XTC Probability is above 0.
typical_p: Locally typical sampling. Keeps tokens whose probability is close to the expected information content, favoring 'typical' text. 1.0 disables it.
repeat_last_n: Number of most recent tokens checked for the repetition penalty. 0 disables it; -1 uses the whole context.
repeat_penalty: Penalizes tokens that appeared recently to reduce repetition. 1.0 is no penalty; values like 1.1-1.2 discourage repeating, but too high can hurt coherence.
presence_penalty: Flat penalty applied to any token that has already appeared, encouraging new topics. 0 disables it; positive values increase novelty.
frequency_penalty: Penalty that grows with how often a token has appeared, reducing word repetition. 0 disables it; positive values reduce repetition.
dry_multiplier: Strength of the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) sequence-repetition penalty. 0 disables it; typical values are around 0.8.
dry_base: Base for the exponential DRY penalty. Higher values penalize longer repeated sequences more steeply. Only used when DRY Multiplier is above 0.
dry_allowed_length: Longest repeated sequence (in tokens) allowed before the DRY penalty starts. Longer repeats get penalized exponentially.
dry_penalty_last_n: How many recent tokens DRY scans for repeats. 0 disables it; -1 uses the whole context.
mirostat: Mirostat sampling mode that keeps output perplexity steady. 0 = off, 1 = Mirostat, 2 = Mirostat 2.0. When enabled, it overrides top-k, top-p and similar samplers.
mirostat_tau: Mirostat target entropy. Lower values give more focused, coherent text; higher values give more diverse text.
mirostat_eta: Mirostat learning rate. Controls how quickly it adjusts to feedback. Lower is slower and more stable; higher is more responsive.
adaptive_target: Target probability for adaptive sampling, which steers the output toward this value. Negative values (-1) disable it.
adaptive_decay: Decay rate for adaptive sampling's running history. Higher values react more slowly and smoothly; lower values adapt faster.
max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens to generate in the response. -1 means no limit (until the end of the response or the context is full).
n_predict: Maximum number of tokens to predict. -1 means unlimited. Same purpose as Max Tokens.
n_keep: Number of tokens from the start of the prompt to always keep when the context overflows. 0 keeps none; -1 keeps all.
n_discard: Number of tokens to discard when the context is full and shifts. 0 uses the default (half of the non-kept context).
ignore_eos: If enabled, the model ignores the end-of-sequence token and keeps generating until the token limit is reached.
stream: If enabled, tokens are sent as they are generated instead of waiting for the full response.
n_probs: Number of top token probabilities returned for each generated token. 0 disables it. Useful for debugging.
min_keep: Minimum number of tokens that must remain after sampling filters (top-k, top-p, min-p, etc.). 0 means no minimum.
chat_format: Format used to parse and render chat messages and tool calls. 'Content-only' treats the output as plain text.
reasoning_format: How the model's reasoning ('thinking') is handled. 'none' leaves it unparsed in the response; other options extract it into a separate field.
reasoning_in_content: If enabled, reasoning text is kept inside the main response content instead of a separate reasoning field.
speculative.types: Type of speculative decoding used to speed up generation with draft predictions. 'none' disables it.
timings_per_token: If enabled, timing information (speed, latency) is returned for each generated token.
post_sampling_probs: If enabled, returned token probabilities are those after the sampling filters were applied, rather than the raw model probabilities.
backend_sampling: If enabled, sampling runs on the backend (e.g. GPU) instead of the CPU, which can improve speed on supported setups.
lora: List of LoRA adapters to apply, each with an ID and scale. An empty list means none are applied.
